Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! New Zealand players are making their way out to the middle now and spread out to take their respective field positions.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

New Zealand will feel they're at least 30 runs short of what could have been a competitive total. They'll need early wickets now if they are to put pressure on the hosts. Sri Lanka on the other hand, will back themselves to chase this down. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Sadeera Samarawickrama is up for a quick chat. He says that it was a pretty good fielding effort from the team. Adds that it is tough out there with the dew but everyone worked hard and it is showing. Mentions that he takes his fielding very seriously and always tries to improve on that. Says that their fielding coach, Upul Chandana was a great fielder in his time and he wants them to stop at lease 15-20 in each game and grab a few half-chances as well.

After losing 4 wickets for below 100, Mark Chapman and Mitchell Hay batted brilliantly and revived the New Zealand innings. When they were batting, 250 looked possible. However, Fernando in the 37th over managed to get Chapman and Michael Bracewell and from then on, the lower order crumbled too.

A really good performance with the ball by Sri Lanka! They really made the Kiwis work hard for their runs and also managed to take timely wickets. It was the spinners who did a good job at the start. Dunith Wellalage, Maheesh Theekshana and Jeffrey Vandersay really were good in the first phase of the innings. It was Asitha Fernando though who actually bowled the over which took his side right on top.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Maheesh Theekshana wraps things up and Mitchell Hay has been dismissed on 49. Flatter, full and around off, Hay goes down for the reverse sweep but misses as the ball passes very close to the bat and his gloves. There is a huge appeal by the Lankans and they look confident as there is a small noise. However, the umpire says no. Charith Asalanka takes the review, UtraEdge shows a spike when the ball is close to the gloves and the on-field call is overturned. To be fair, even before the decision came on the big screen, Hay started to walk back, and only the umpire was on the field to raise his finger. New Zealand have been bowled out for 209!

Nathan Smith tries to work it across the line but plays down the wrong line and misses getting hit on the front pad first, then the back pad. There is a huge appeal for LBW, and up goes the finger. PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof is pitchside. He says that the fitness levels of the players will be tested as it is very hot and humid. New Zealand, on the other hand, got off to a promising start in the shortened chase, but their innings fell apart after the dismissals of openers Will Young and Tim Robinson. While Michael Bracewell showed some resilience, players like Glenn Phillips and Mark Chapman will need to step up and take more responsibility. With the ball, Mitchell Santner and Ish Sodhi remain key threats but must focus on maintaining consistency in their line and length. The weather seems a bit uncertain, but we’re hopeful for some action, even if it’s a reduced game. Stay tuned for the toss and more updates!

Sri Lanka has had a remarkable year across formats, excelling in T20Is, ODIs, and Tests, where they remain in contention for the WTC final. Kusal Mendis and Avishka Fernando set the tone for the series with centuries in the opening match, and the team will once again rely on them to provide a strong start. The middle order has been consistently reliable, adding depth to their batting lineup. On the bowling front, Maheesh Theekshana and Dunith Wellalage will be key players, especially on a spin-friendly pitch.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of the 2nd ODI between Sri Lanka and New Zealand at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. Sri Lanka leads the series 1-0 after an impressive performance in the first match. Meanwhile, New Zealand will be eager to bounce back and level the series with a win here.
... MATCH DAY ...

After an entertaining Dambulla leg of New Zealand's white-ball tour of Sri Lanka, the action now shifts south to the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy for the final two ODIs. The three-match series stands at 1-0 in favour of the hosts, who are eager to extend their impressive home streak, having remained unbeaten in series across formats since September. In the rain-affected opening game, centuries from Avishka Fernando and Kusal Mendis powered Sri Lanka to an imposing total. Chasing a revised target of 221 runs in 27 overs, New Zealand fell significantly short. The absence of Lockie Ferguson, ruled out of the series due to a calf injury, exposed the inexperience in their pace attack. However, the inclusion of Adam Milne as Ferguson’s replacement adds much-needed experience and stability. On the batting front, the Kiwis had two debutants among their six batters, and their vulnerability against spin as a team was evident. To stay alive in the series, the likes of Will Young, Henry Nicholls, and Glenn Phillips must step up and deliver impactful performances. As for Sri Lanka, they were near flawless in the opening game, with their batters setting a strong foundation and the bowlers complementing with disciplined spells. They haven’t secured qualification for the 2025 Champions Trophy but a series win here would boost their morale and reaffirm their dominance at home. Unless there are last-minute injury concerns, the hosts are likely to stick with the same playing XI. Should they seal the series in this second ODI, they may look to rotate players and rest key members ahead of the Test series in South Africa later this month. That said, Charith Asalanka and Co. would not want to look too far ahead and their focus would be firmly on clinching the series. Can the Kiwis muster a spirited comeback to level the series, or will the hosts assert their dominance and seal the series? We shall find out soon enough.
